annotator_1_reasoning: admindocs renders view/model docstrings through docutils. Django's own docstrings start with an empty first line so the first content line carries the block's indentation and the minimum comes out right; but for the common style where text begins immediately after the opening quotes, the first line's indentation is zero, the computed common indent is zero, and the continuation lines are returned still carrying their source indentation. When parse_rst then embeds this text beneath the '.. default-role:: cmsreference' directive it prepends, docutils treats the indented lines as content of that directive, and since default-role permits no content it emits a system-message error block instead of the rendered docstring — so admindoc pages error on any docstring whose first line is non-empty.

The net effect is that adding db_collation to a primary key leaves every referencing foreign key column at its old collation, producing mismatched-collation FK constraint failures on MySQL and stale column definitions elsewhere.

Django's ServerHandler subclass customizes header cleanup and connection lifecycle but nothing about HEAD, so from 1.10 onward curl -iX HEAD against runserver receives the full HTML body after the headers (and compliant clients that hang up after headers produce 'Broken pipe' errors in the console).
